questions.question: What is chain of custody?
questions.solution_html:
• The chain of custody is the documented and unbroken transfer record of evidence
  • from the scene to the court, ensuring its integrity and admissibility. ((2 marks))
questions.final_answer: The chain of custody is the documented and unbroken transfer record of evidence
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the principle of the chromotropic acid test for detecting methyl alcohol
questions.solution_html:
• Chromotropic acid test detects formaldehyde (formed by oxidation of methanol). In
  • presence of conc. H₂SO₄, chromotropic acid reacts with formaldehyde to give a
  • purple/violet colour. ((2 marks))
questions.final_answer: purple/violet colour. ()

questions.question: What is the principle of Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC)?
questions.solution_html:
• TLC is based on differential adsorption of compounds on a stationary phase
  • (silica/alumina) and their movement with a mobile phase (solvent). ((2 marks))
questions.final_answer: TLC is based on differential adsorption of compounds on a stationary phase

questions.question: What is the Rhodamine test? How is it used in dye examination?
questions.solution_html:
• Rhodamine test detects synthetic dyes. The dye extracts give fluorescent pink
  • coloration under UV when treated with rhodamine B reagent — used to compare
  • textile or fibre dyes. (Principle – 1, Procedure – 2, Forensic use – 1)
  • 25900405

questions.question: Describe how solid-phase extraction can be applied for drug evidence purification.
questions.solution_html:
• In SPE, the analyte is retained on a solid adsorbent column; impurities are washed
  • off, and analyte is eluted. Used for drug purification before GC/MS or HPLC
  • analysis. (Mark distribution- Principle – 1, Procedure/steps – 2, Forensic use – 1)
questions.final_answer: analysis. (Mark distribution- Principle – 1, Procedure/steps – 2, Forensic use – 1)
